intro: CSV to HTML Table converts CSV text into a clean HTML <table> with a <thead> for the first row and a <tbody> for the remaining rows. It's handy when you need to drop tabular data into a web page, email, or documentation without writing the markup by hand. Paste your CSV and copy the generated table markup.
useCases: Embed a spreadsheet export as a static HTML table in a blog post or docs page
Generate table markup for an email or CMS that accepts raw HTML
Quickly preview how comma-separated data maps to header and body rows
Turn a small dataset into HTML for a prototype or mockup
Produce escaped, copy-paste-ready table markup without hand-typing tags

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript, and nothing is uploaded or stored on any server. The site is open source so you can verify this.

faq.q: How is the first row handled?
faq.a: The first CSV row becomes the table header inside <thead> using <th> cells. Every following row becomes a <tr> of <td> cells inside <tbody>.

faq.q: Does it escape special HTML characters?
faq.a: Yes. The characters &, < and > in cell values are escaped to &, < and > so the output is safe to drop into HTML and won't break the markup.

faq.q: What delimiters and formats are supported?
faq.a: Parsing is done with PapaParse, which auto-detects the delimiter (such as commas, tabs, or semicolons) and handles quoted fields. Empty lines are skipped automatically.

faq.q: What happens if the CSV is empty or invalid?
faq.a: If there are no rows after trimming and skipping empty lines, you'll see a "No data to convert" error. Fatal parse errors are also reported instead of producing broken output.
